l.i: Anthedon, ubi gramineo de littore Glaucus
Poscentes irrupit aquas, iam crine, genisque
Caerulus, & mixtos expauit ab inguine pisces.
Glandibus, & torta Zephiros incidere funda
Cura, Cydonaeas anteibunt gasa sagittas.
Tu quoque praeclarum forma Cephise dedisses
Narcissum: sed Thespiacis iam pallet in agris
Trux puer, orbata florem pater alluit unda:
Quis tibi Phoebeas acies? veterémque renoluat
Phocida? quis Panopen? quis Aulida? quis Cyparissson?
Et valles Lebadaea tuas, & Hyampolin acri
Submissam scopulo? vel qui Parnassson utrúnque,
Aut Cyrrham tauris, Aenemoreámque supinant,
Coryciumque nemus? propellentémque Lileam
Cephisi glaciale caput, quo suetus anhelam
Ferre sitim Pytho, amnémque auertere ponto.
Omnibus immixtas cono super aspice lauros,
Armáque, vel Tityon, vel Delon habentia, vel quas
Hic deus innumera laxauit cade pharetras.
Iphitus acer agit genitor, cui nuper ademptus
Naubolus Hippasides.
Orbe pererrato (quis enim deprendere posset
Furta Iouis?) profugus patriámque, irámque parentis
Vitat Agenorides, Phoebíque oracula supplex
Consulit, & qua sit tellus habitanda, requirit.
Bos tibi, Phoebus ait, Solis occurret in aruis,
Nullum passa iugum, curuíque immunis aratri:
Hac duce carpe vias, & qua requieuerit herba,
Moenia fac condas, Boeotiáque illa vocato.
Vix bene Castalio Cadmus descenderat antro:
Incustoditam lentè videt ire inuencam.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right are partly faint and abbreviated; readings of "Cephisus fl.", "Thespia op." and "Anthedon" are uncertain. Lines are set as verse; the final line is cut off at the foot of the page. The signature "I 2" at the foot is treated as a gathering mark and omitted from the text.
